headline: Quantifying sequencing error in targeted and low-coverage assays
label: Sequencing Error Modelling Methods
summary: Recent preprints and papers model platform-specific error in targeted amplicon, repeat, and low-coverage methylation sequencing.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit modelling of error and platform behaviour in targeted and low-coverage sequencing. CHARLIE locates interruptions within expanded repeats from Illumina and PacBio targeted sequencing and profiles platform-specific errors. PASTA applies a count-based statistical framework to quantify and confirm chromosomal translocation junctions from targeted amplicon sequencing. Sparse-Seq shows that low-coverage sequencing can quantify genome-wide 5mC and 5hmC with predictable error, and provides an online error-calculation tool. The rice long-read RNA-seq study is a less direct fit: it attributes most plant fusion transcripts to artifacts, mainly RT template switching, and proposes a validation pipeline. The 9p21 chromatin study and the nucDetective Plasmodium analysis address regulatory architecture rather than measurement error and sit outside this thread. What is new here is the treatment of error as a modelled, quantifiable parameter in sequencing-based measurement.
